methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $15M total raised proxy.

private.name: Cobod
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Material Evolution is a Series A-stage housing and construction company founded by Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark. The company has raised $15M to date. The comparable universe for valuation is limited, comprising one identified private peer (Cobod) and no public comparables in the sector.

Stage-progression analysis, the only methodologically applicable triangulation approach given data constraints, applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy. This method assumes typical Series A to subsequent-stage step-up dynamics and yields an implied post-money valuation of $30M. The limited comp set constrains our ability to cross-validate this result through revenue or EBITDA multiples.

The triangulated valuation range is $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median of $30M. This relatively narrow band reflects the application of a single method rather than convergence across multiple independent approaches. Key uncertainties include the thinness of comparable data in frontier construction tech, the absence of public market benchmarks for sector valuation multiples, and potential divergence between the company's growth trajectory and historical stage-progression assumptions. Additional revenue, customer, or unit economics data would be needed to strengthen confidence in any valuation within this range.
